title: Canonical strict derived-limit comparison for exact product-preserving module functors
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites with sheaves of commutative rings $R,S$, and put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ and $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Mod}(S)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume countable products in both categories are exact. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive and exact and assume its canonical countable-product comparison $\phi:F(\prod_nM_n)\to\prod_nF(M_n)$, characterized by $\mathrm{pr}_n\phi=F(\mathrm{pr}_n)$, is an isomorphism for every family. Write $F_D$ for its termwise derived functor [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], and $F^{\operatorname{Tow}}_D$ for termwise application to complexes of strict towers [def-weil-inverse-system, lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Let $L_{\mathcal A},L_{\mathcal B}$ be total right derived inverse limit [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit].

There is a natural isomorphism
$$\lambda_M:F_D L_{\mathcal A}M\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{\mathcal B}F^{\operatorname{Tow}}_D M.$$
It is the following specified comparison. For a strict tower complex $M$ with transition shift $s$, put $P_M=\prod_nM_n$ termwise and let $H_M^q=P_M^q\oplus P_M^{q-1}$ with differential $d(x,y)=(dx,(1-s)x-dy)$. Use the normalized natural Roos isomorphism of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison], in these signed coordinates, to write $\theta_M:L_{\mathcal A}M\xrightarrow{\sim}H_M$; its K-injective normalization is $z\mapsto(\iota z,0)$. If $\kappa_M:F_DH_M\to H_{FM}$ is the map $\phi$ on both summands, then
$$\lambda_M=\theta_{FM}^{-1}\kappa_M F_D(\theta_M).$$
This equals the comparison obtained by preserving the ordinary inverse limit and then resolving the image tower: for $M\to I$ K-injective and $F I\to J$ a K-injective target resolution, it is represented by $F\lim I\cong\lim F I\to\lim J$ and the inverse of the derived image of $FM\to FI$. It is independent of those resolutions. For the specified Roos triangles, with first maps $p,p'$ and connecting maps $\delta,\delta'$, and the shift comparison $\xi$, it satisfies
$$p'\lambda_M=\phi F_D(p),\qquad\lambda_M[1]\xi F_D(\delta)=\delta'\phi.$$
For every complex $C$ and strict augmentation $\gamma:\Delta C\to M$, it carries $F_D$ of the canonical derived map $C\to L_{\mathcal A}M$ induced by $\gamma$ to the canonical derived map $F_DC\to L_{\mathcal B}FM$ induced by $F\gamma$. Here $\Delta C$ is the constant tower; both maps are those of the normalized Roos comparison, equivalently of the constant-tower/derived-limit adjunction.

Preservation of countable products and equalizers implies preservation of tower limits by Mathlib. Apply this degreewise to complexes and take preservesLimitIso; its projection equation proves the beta normalization.
Descend the normalized chain comparison and identify it on every pair of K-injective resolutions.
Apply the strict-coordinate triangle and augmentation compatibility calculation to this same lambda and assemble all clauses.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q42-97f476e3e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS with no changes: the nine steps are correct, every hypothesis is met, and the delivery adds no new nodes. Statement: unchanged and no weaker than what its citers use, which are Steps 6 and 11 of lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison and Steps 3 and 10 of thm-cbc-complete-proetale. They use the signed Roos model with lambda = theta^-1 kappa F(theta), the two triangle equations and the strict-augmentation clause. Coefficients are Mod(R) and Mod(S) on small sites, both with exact countable products. Step checks: Step 2's signs follow from the cone convention of def-weil-abstract-derived-category; changing (u,v) to (v,-u) gives d(x,y)=(dx,(1-s)x-dy), and the Roos inclusion (0,iota z) becomes (iota z,0). Steps 3 and 5 hold because kappa is block diagonal and F is additive. Step 7: I recomputed a_J(lim r)beta_I = H(r)kappa_I F(a_I) by components; the n-th product component is r_n F(pi_n) and the shifted component is 0. With theta_{FI} = H(r)^-1 a_J this gives lambda_I = (lim r)beta_I. Step 8: the argument for arbitrary K-injective resolutions uses only what the 070I node states (bijection into K-injectives, homotopy equivalences). Step 9: the augmentation clause gives (F gamma_n, 0). Applying resolution existence on the tower site matches Step 1 of lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit and Stacks 0941, which I read at sites-cohomology.tex lines 5067-5107; I also confirmed the cited tags 07KC and 070I in the tag table. Edge cases: F=id gives identities; zero transitions make both sides 0. With F = -⊗Q on Ab and the tower Z <-p- Z, (R^1 lim)⊗Q is nonzero while the image tower Q <-p- Q has Rlim = Q, so the product hypothesis is necessary. Duplicates: none in the DAG. lem-cbc-exact-functor-rlim is pro-etale and existence only; lem-pc-derived-functor-commutes-derived-limit has no canonical map; lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison is about direct images, not an exact functor. theorem exactProductFunctorStrictLimit
    {C : Type uC} [Category.{vC} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{max uC vC r}]
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max uC vC r}]
    (R : Sheaf J RingCat.{max uC vC r})
    {D : Type uD} [Category.{vD} D] (K : GrothendieckTopology D)
    [HasSheafify K AddCommGrpCat.{max uD vD s}]
    [K.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max uD vD s}]
    (S : Sheaf K RingCat.{max uD vD s})
    (_hR : ∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ) (a b : R.obj.obj U), a * b = b * a)
    (_hS : ∀ (U : Dᵒᵖ) (a b : S.obj.obj U), a * b = b * a)
    [HasExactLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) (ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r} R)]
    [HasExactLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) (ringedSiteModules.{max uD vD s} S)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wA} (ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r} R)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wA} (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r} R)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wB} (ringedSiteModules.{max uD vD s} S)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wB} (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ringedSiteModules.{max uD vD s} S)]
    (F : ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r} R ⥤ ringedSiteModules.{max uD vD s} S)
    [F.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits F] [PreservesFiniteColimits F]
    (_hphi : ∀ (M : ℕ → ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r} R), IsIso (piComparison F M))
    (LA : DerivedCategory.{wA} (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r} R) ⥤ DerivedCategory.{wA}
      (ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r} R))
    (LB : DerivedCategory.{wB} (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ringedSiteModules.{max uD vD s} S) ⥤ DerivedCategory.{wB}
      (ringedSiteModules.{max uD vD s} S))
    (etaA : HomologicalComplex.complexOfFunctorsToFunctorToComplex ⋙
      (lim : (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ CochainComplex (ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r} R) ℤ) ⥤ CochainComplex
        (ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r} R) ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q.{wA} ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q.{wA} ⋙
        LA)
    (_hLA : LA.IsRightDerivedFunctor etaA
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ringedSiteModules.{max uC vC r} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (etaB : HomologicalComplex.complexOfFunctorsToFunctorToComplex ⋙
      (lim : (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ CochainComplex (ringedSiteModules.{max uD vD s} S) ℤ) ⥤ CochainComplex
        (ringedSiteModules.{max uD vD s} S) ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q.{wB} ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q.{wB} ⋙
        LB)
    (_hLB : LB.IsRightDerivedFunctor etaB
      (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ringedSiteModules.{max uD vD s} S) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))) :
